combiner: SHA-256(x25519_ss || mlkem_ss); both halves are 32 bytes; output is a 32-byte hybrid shared secret. This is a model combiner, not X-Wing and not RFC 10024; see docs/HYBRID_KEM.md.

controls.C-1: all-zero X25519 peer key rejected by OpenSSL EVP (rc=-1); the hybrid cannot complete with a zero X25519 part
controls.C-2: tampered ML-KEM ciphertext decapsulates to a different shared secret (implicit rejection); hybrid secret differs from reference
controls.C-3: tampered X25519 shared secret changes the hybrid secret

design: H-1 concatenated hybrid KEM: client sends X25519 ephemeral public key and ML-KEM ciphertext; server derives X25519 and decapsulates ML-KEM; both combine with SHA-256. Verification accepts only when both halves complete (AND policy).
measured_source: outputs/hybrid_bench.log sections B and C (n=200, single thread)

fields.name: mlkem_ciphertext
fields.value: ML-KEM ciphertext for the server public key

wire_format.note: Every byte of this format is fixed above; there are no unspecified bytes and no open design decisions in H-1. The server ML-KEM public key (800 / 1184 / 1568 bytes) is distributed out of band with the peer identity material (see docs/HYBRID_KEM.md open decision D-01 on distribution channel).

x25519_only_reference.note: 2 x X25519 derive at 65.32 us each (measured, outputs/hybrid_bench.log section A); hybrid overhead vs X25519-only is total_us minus 130.64 us
